newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-LARA FINALLY LIVES UP TO REPUTATION.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-LARA FINALLY LIVES UP TO REPUTATION.

text.p: Brian Lara finally lived up to his reputation by scoring his first century of the test series as West Indies built a substantial lead over Australia in the fifth and final test on Sunday.
The West Indies vice-captain and number four batsman banished memories of a disappointing tour with an inspired 132 on the second day at the WACA Ground.

His innings, which gradually increased in tempo and flamboyance after a cautious beginning, helped steer the tourists to a 353 for seven, a lead of 110 runs, in reply to Australia's first innings 243 at close of play.
Carl Hooper remained unbeaten on 57, including ten fours, alongside tail-ender Ian Bishop on five not out.

Lara's century, his only first-class hundred on tour, provided just reward for his unusually patient approach early on after joining opener Robert Samuels in a crucial partnerhip that lifted West Indies out of trouble.
Brought together with the fall of Shivnarine Chanderpaul for three with the total on 43 for two, the pair added 208 runs for the third wicket, the biggest West Indies partnership of the series.

Lara's dismal form on tour -- the world record holder for the highest score in test cricket averaged just 20 in eight previous test innings -- proved a key factor in Australia taking an unassailable 3-1 lead to retain the Frank Worrell trophy.
Samuels provided a perfect foil for Lara, taking five-and-a-half hours and 228 deliveries to reach 76, his highest score of the test series.
In contrast, Lara faced 185 deliveries and smashed 22 fours and one six during his stay of nearly four hours at the crease.
Although he cut loose after reaching his century, saving his most aggressive shots for leg-spinner Shane Warne, it was Lara's early approach that differed sharply from his previous efforts.
Until now, Lara has appeared determined to dominate the bowling from the outset, whatever the circumstances, a tactic that failed to pay dividends for him or his team.
In an apparent change of approach, Lara was highly cautious in his shot selection while playing himself in, shedding the cuts and pulls that have so often led to his downfall on tour.
Australia captain Mark Taylor set a field of three slips and three gulleys to greet Lara but he refused to be tempted into launching a premature attack.
That all changed after Lara reached three figures just before tea, an achievement he acknowledged by raising both arms in the air before receiving a celebratory hug from Samuels.
After being hit by Lara for 26 runs in 14 balls, including four fours and one six, Warne gained revenge in the 72nd over of the innings.
Lara, who scored two limited overs centuries on tour, pushed forward defensively to a wide delivery only to edge a catch to wicketkeeper Ian Healy.
Warne added a second wicket to his tally by removing Samuels, who was caught off the gloves by Mark Waugh at silly point. Pace bowler Paul Reiffel then took three quick wickets.
West Indies began the day on 25 for no wicket before losing opener Sherwin Campbell and Chanderpual cheaply before lunch.
Fast bowler Curtly Ambrose underlined his importance to the tourists by taking five for 43 on Saturday on his return from injury, while Waugh and Michael Bevan both scored fine half-centuries.
